title: My boyfriend finally made his first game
author: TinyStressBall
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I hope this post is allowed. I’m writing this because I want to give my boyfriend’s passion project a honest chance.

For as long as I’ve known him, he’s wanted to make a game. But between handling life and the overwhelming coding a game requires, he could never get past the initial setup phase. We do believe he has undiagnosed ADHD so that might have played a role in him being unable to commit until a game reaches the final product phase. With the new available AI tools, he finally managed to build and finish a complete, playable web game: [amongdemons.com](https://amongdemons.com) . Using AI has allowed him to guide "someone" else to write all those thousands of lines of code while he could simply guide, check the implementation and bugfix.

A couple of days ago, he tried sharing it on Reddit, and the comments completely shredded him because of AI use. Like viscerally "you're a garbage human being" type of comments. Never even tried the game for a second. It was genuinely painful to watch. While he did use AI art and AI tools to make this a finished product, he's invested around 4 months of genuine work into this and it deserves at least a try.

We both worked on getting the artwork done with AI which was interesting to navigate when considering we wanted to keep a certain aesthetic. We used a locally installed image generation software and we have really bad PCs so it wasn't one of the good ones, haha. I remember we kept using the seeds to try to get similar artwork. I wish I remembered what we used but that was about a year ago and then we rekindled our interest in among demons earlier this year.

Since early 2026 he's heard of Codex and wanted to give it a try. He used it to code his initial versions and was mind blown with what it can do. While there were limits to a web game in terms of what animations it could do, we still think it did a decent job with that dynamic feel a game should have.   
  
When the game was done we needed a video presentation for Steam, so he went ahead and recorded some game mechanics then asked Codex to create a dynamic video presentation because we both absolutely suck at video editing. We honestly didn't believe it'd be able to achieve anything, but we got a decent result out of it (even though it's something a beginner would probably put out). We're fine with it.

That being said about how we used AI, I won’t sit here and claim it’s a masterpiece since it’s his very first release, and it has its rough edges. But me and our friend group have been genuinely hooked playing it lately, and it turned out to be a fun experience for us. I've been loving completing my collection and the back and forth with who's top of the leaderboard with our friends.

If you have a few free minutes and like checking out indie web games and don't have an innate hate of AI use, I’d love it if you gave it a try. It would mean the world to him to see people actually playing it. 

If you're feeling extra generous and you enjoy the game, he also ported it to an executable and put it on steam at the whopping price of 2.99$ It's not necessary to buy anything though as you can play for free on the web. You'll get a nice badge saying you supported the game, though! :)

replies.author: First-Tutor-5454
replies.body: Confused, you're using AI anyway, can it not make sprites and do animations?

replies.author: TinyStressBall
replies.body: We couldn't get it to. No.

replies.author: First-Tutor-5454
replies.body: A sprite sheet is just the same character in different poses. Animation is just putting them in a certain order based on what is happening (swinging a sword etc). I haven't tried using AI in game development but am surprised to hear it can't do this

replies.author: TinyStressBall
replies.body: As far as our experience goes it doesn't know how to generate images that would work in sequence. It keeps changing things slightly so it doesn't work as a sprite. There's probably some AI out there that's specifically for that use and has been trained in that regard, but the one we were using was impressive in coding capabilities, decent in simple art generation and video editing, really bad at every attempt at a sprite. Maybe there's AI tools that you can run locally which are amazing at that but our PCs are quite old and wouldn't be able to run any of that.

comments.author: Borg453
comments.body:
Good luck. I like the aesthetic and the relaxed feeling of the game. 

For feedback, I think the game has a lot of systems to take in. First i semi-skipped the tutorial, and found that i could only beat one encounter. Then I completed the tutorial, and started trying to collect creatures from the dungeon, which tbh. feels a bit grindy.. but perhaps its because my options arent all that clear. 

I'm more of a tactical player, than a resource collector - so perhaps that is why i dont get all the sub systems: The gameplay loop appears something like this. Amass an army to defeat encounters on the world map.. to amass an army you need to play the dungeon game:  
dungeon -> extract defeated units -> convert to essence -> gather enough essence to craft potion -> get enough potions to create a variant of the monster.. or upgrade them, so you can create a better one, but that then requires even more potions to craft a more powerful version.

There is something in the milestones or directions that I dont get.. so there wasnt a clear apparent path for me to take other than upgrade a, to b and then to c (which, if i am brash just like unlucking goal posts). Perhaps because I am tired. 

I guess my hesitance is that this game feels very based on crafting: convert resource a into b. When you have enough b, you can get c.. you might use c.. but you could also spend even more time, until you get d.

There is certainly an audience for this - so I say: keep up the good work. 

I really like the world map, and for the most part, the UI is pretty straight forward.

I work as a UX'er and i do game design as a hobby. Don't let negativity get your duo down.

replies.author: TinyStressBall
replies.body: Thank you! Your insight is much appreciated!

replies.author: Borg453

comments.author: num1d1um

I'd ask if this was tested but of course I know the answer is no, and I also know nobody actually thought about the balancing values and tutorial flow. This is what happens when you put out low effort slop, you have no idea what's actually going on inside your game, because you become an observer, a consumer of your own product. The UI and UX are identical to the 500 other vibe coded creature fighter games out there. The creature artwork is gaudy and generic.

replies.author: TinyStressBall
replies.body:
We do test and try to fix the bugs as best we can. See, that's exactly the "already made up my mind" type of attitude I feel has no place. Even if he used AI, we've been actively playing the game and doing bug fixes and such as we find them and as our friends report them to us.  
  
Yes, I know balancing isn't the best because it's a first game and we don't know much about balancing and game design. He's doing his best to learn and adjust.

We'll have another look at the tutorial and see if we can replicate and find a fix. :) While you didn't really try to give constructive criticism but instead just called it low effort slop, I'll just go ahead and take the valuable information out of your comment. So thanks for that, I guess.

comments.author: perelmanych
comments.body: Big shoutout to you for supporting your bf, instead of bitching him for spending time on stupid things, if you are real of course, lol.

replies.author: TinyStressBall
replies.body:
The "spending time on stupid stuff" narative is something I always hated and if anyone's girlfriend ever acts annoyed because they have hobbies maybe there's a need to reconsider the relationship. I had highschool friends who would say that about their boyfriends and I couldn't understand how a hobby could make them so annoyed. If they're neglecting important parts of life then sure, have a talk but otherwise wth.

It probably also helps that we have common interests. We both were doing freelance web development for a while, we're both into gaming, etc.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
Whilst there is a lot of bandwagon AI hate I don't think anyone needs to play the game to have an opinion on it, they can just watch the video.

To be completely blunt the art looks like generic AI art, the UI looks like every other AI game and the gameplay is basically just watching some images battle other images with numbers appearing. These type of games can appeal to some people but it's a niche.

Generally the game just looks like it was made by someone with no art skills, no design skills and likely no programming skills. Then on top of that for some reason you have paid to put it on Steam in the hope of making some money. All that is going to give people a bad impression straight off the bat because it comes across as something that's been created almost entirely by AI.

It's not been used to help you make a game, it's been used to make a game for you and it shows.

In the end the main thing is that you both had fun creating it but having ADHD isn't going to shield anyone online from being criticized.

For the next one try and use AI as more of a tool than a crutch. Coding isn't as important unless it runs badly or it's full of bugs but art and design is going to stick out. Try and put more manual effort into that part and people will probably be more forgiving. 

Generally if it looks like something obviously made made with AI then you've failed and need to put in more effort. Ideally you want to aim for creating a game that nobody can even know any AI was used without you telling them.

replies.author: TinyStressBall
replies.body:
Sure, but see you gave reasons and you were civil. Big difference. I guess for us if we enjoy the game and people around us still play after weeks then there's something there. Would shitty artwork that we can do ourselves make it better? I honestly don't think so. But that's just my opinion knowing the limited skill we both have in that.

He put it on steam not to get rich, trust me he spent way more on AI these months than a small game at this price could cover but I understand it being perceived like that however he also has a free web version with all the same features, nothing paywalled. So yeah. 

Maybe we did make a game for ourselves then. And that's fine too. I'll continue playing it. Just thought if we like it there might be more people like us. That's all.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
Well Reddit isn't really a civil place most of the time, especially in bigger subs, people like to see everything as black and white and jump on bandwagons. 

For the art you should look into learning a bit of basic editing. When I use generative AI I like to use it more like photobashing so you're essentially taking bits from different images and blending them together in something like Gimp or Photoshop then you can combine that with some paint over and post work and you can remove the generic AI look a lot of the time and you don't need to be a great artist.

You could also look into things like the Krita add-on that lets you draw and then send that through AI, you don't need to be a great artist for that either. Anything that gets you away from just prompting images is going to help avoid the instant anti AI kneejerk reactions, at least the legitimate ones anyway. It's the visuals that people are mostly reacting negatively to.

replies.body: Appreciate the insight on how we could use AI in that sense for artwork. Thank you
